The core mathematical framework for analyzing Leicester's 2015/16 Premier League triumph involves a dual-component decomposition of performance deviation into skill and luck residuals. The Pythagorean expectation model with β = 1.24208 is used to estimate expected win probability based on goals scored and conceded. The actual performance is then compared against this baseline to compute a Z-score representing deviation. The luck component (Z_Luck = 1.355616) reflects stochastic overperformance, while the skill component (Z_Skill = 2.663975986) captures systematic improvements in tactical execution and player performance. These are combined as Z_Total = Z_Skill + Z_Luck = 4.019591986, which corresponds to an extremely low probability (15,000:1) under the null hypothesis of pure chance. This implies that while luck played a role, the overwhelming majority of the deviation is attributable to skill-based factors. The failure mode lies in assuming independence between skill and luck components, which may not hold if certain tactical innovations amplify random fluctuations.
